Thanks Claire — this is exactly the kind of detail we need. Quick answers and plan: 

- Short bursts: Hosted supports short burst capacity (burst credit model) — we can absorb 500 RPS for 30–90s depending on concurrent token rates, but repeated sustained bursts (many times per hour) should be modeled separately.
- Sustained 400 RPS: possible on Hosted for mixed request sizes, but cost and latency predictability improve with Dedicated if the baseline is sustained and latency SLOs are tight. We can provide a cost sketch once you fill the pilot-plan.xlsx.
- SOC2 / VPC: For the pilot (sandbox), we can provide SOC2 evidence and a scoped runbook; production VPC/private deployment is available as Dedicated or Private.

Subject: Technical deep-dive: sandbox endpoints, rate controls, and recommended test plan

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the context. Short technical notes ahead of the sync and a suggested test plan you can follow in the sandbox: 

Sandbox endpoints (readonly):
- https://sandbox.redwood.ai/finlytics/v1/generate — "generate" endpoint for completions
- https://sandbox.redwood.ai/finlytics/v1/embed — "embed" endpoint for embeddings

Credentials: we'll provision ephemeral API keys scoped to the sandbox (see attached sandbox-credentials.txt).

Rate controls & behavior:
- Default hosted rate cap: 200 RPS per endpoint per API key for the sandbox.
- Burst behavior: short bursts up to 500 RPS are allowed via our burst pool; however, sustained 400 RPS for hours is considered baseline capacity and recommended to evaluate for Dedicated.
- Concurrency: aim for <= 50 concurrent open streams for best latency stability on high-token completions (1–2k tokens). Use streaming for longer outputs to reduce client-side timeouts.

Performance knobs we recommend you test in the pilot:
1) Prefix/KV caching of repeated system prompts (will lower tokens/token-cost and improve tail latency).
2) Batch small requests where possible (we can demo continuous batching).
3) Adjust max_tokens to trade off quality vs latency.

Sample curl to validate throughput (replace API_KEY):
curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/finlytics/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3b","prompt":"Summarize: <document>","max_tokens":300}'

Suggested pilot cadence: 2 weeks, with:
- Week 1: synthetic load tests (concurrency + burst), KV cache setup, latency baselining
- Week 2: sampled production traffic (anonymized), quality evaluation, cost sketch

I'll bring example KV config and a short runbook to the call. Proposed meeting: Wed 23 Jun 2027 10:00 PT — does that work?

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
